song.title: You Give Love a Bad Name!

guitar.modelsText: Kramer (Sambora signature, e.g. Wedge/Tour custom) / Ovation acoustic
guitar.evidence: Trained knowledge: Sambora was a long-time Kramer endorser with his own custom guitars; Ovation was commonly used for acoustic ballads.
guitar.notes: Refined to lead with Kramer since that's Sambora's most documented brand association.

tone.target: bright 80s hard-rock crunch with chorus sheen
tone.profile: bright 80s hard-rock crunch with chorus sheen
tone.summary: A classic Plexi-style crunch tone, enhanced by a light Chorus effect and Digital Delay to capture the polished, bright sound of 80s arena rock.
corrections: make it more 80s hard-rock than pop-rock

rig.name: Bon Jovi - You Give Love a Bad Name! - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Clean up hum and background noise.
Provide the necessary crunch and upper-mid punch characteristic of 80s hard rock without excessive distortion.
blocks.gap: The Green OD is used to simulate a light, biting overdrive/boost rather than heavy saturation.

blocks.purpose: Add grit and upper-mid bite for the 'crunch' element, complementing the Green OD.
blocks.gap: Used subtly to enhance crunch rather than as a primary distortion source.

blocks.purpose: Simulate the bright, punchy British Plexi/JCM style amplifier tone.
Provide the classic British 4x12 cabinet sound.
Add the required 'chorus sheen' and 80s polish without sounding overly wet.
Provide the short, polished echo effect required for 80s arena rock.
Add subtle space and polish to the overall tone without sounding like deep reverb.
blocks.gap: Used sparingly to maintain a polished, non-muddy sound.

improvements.summary: Improve cabinet realism for a more authentic, punchy 80s arena rock sound.

proposals.reason: Enhance the upper-mid punch and bite needed for 80s hard rock.
proposals.expectedGain: Increased clarity and definition in the crunch tones.
